prompt: Which feature does the lesson NOT list among the main MANET features?
options: Quality of service for competing traffic
Frequency hopping across channels
Dedicated fixed relay towers
Self-forming, self-healing connectivity
explanation: Page 12 lists self-forming and self-healing, frequency hopping, quality of service, dynamic membership and unicast, multicast and broadcast support. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 12.

prompt: Which list gives the waveforms of the E-LynX shown in the lesson?
options: NB, WB, WMA-HC, STANAG 4204 and SINCGARS
NB, WB, WMA-HC, STANAG 5066 and CNR
NB, WB, WMA-HC, STANAG 4204 and CNR
NB, WB, WMA-LC, STANAG 4204 and CNR
explanation: Page 31 lists the narrowband, wideband, WMA-HC, STANAG 4204 and CNR waveforms. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 31.

prompt: For connectors, the visual inspection looks for which conditions?
options: Fraying, cuts and broken insulation
Damage, corrosion, and broken or bent pins
Cracks and any other external damage
Rough action and interference in the buttons
explanation: Page 25 lists damage, corrosion and broken or bent pins for connectors, while cable inspection covers fraying, cuts and broken insulation. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 25.

prompt: In Net Performance, what does the Dest field specify?
options: The size of the packets to send
The remote ID that the packet is sent to
The pause time between each packet sending
The number of packets received at the destination
explanation: Page 67 describes Dest as the remote ID that the packet is sent to. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 67.

prompt: Which services does the lesson list under data, positions and video integration?
options: Location, data and video
Location, voice and data
Data, voice and video
Location, voice and video
explanation: Page 72 lists location, data and video for the data, positions and video integration. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 72.

prompt: Which MANET feature adapts connectivity when links or members change, helping keep the Common Operational Picture current?
options: Self-forming
Self-healing
Frequency hopping
Concurrent flooding
explanation: Self-healing means adapting connectivity when links or members change; the COP is the shared picture fed by sensor information. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 12; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 9.

prompt: Which protection secures the exchange between a radio and its management station with confidentiality and authentication?
options: Embedded TRANSEC based on AES 256
Over-the-air frequency hopping
The G-10N key fill device
SNMPv3
explanation: Management security is based on SNMPv3, which supports confidentiality and authentication; interoperability still does not mean unrestricted connectivity, so access controls continue to apply. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 30; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24.

prompt: A radio moved outdoors has an intermittent link, and the team suspects environmental effects. Which items does the visual inspection cover?
options: Waveform, node ID, RSSI and SNR
Terrain, temperature and electromagnetic interference
Connectors, casing, controls and cable condition
Software versions, hardware versions and elapsed time
explanation: A visual inspection covers connectors, casing, controls and cable condition; terrain, temperature and EMI are separate environmental factors that affect sensor reliability. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 25; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: Which task can a technician perform from the Test menu of the radio?
options: Load operational parameters under the operator password
Ping another radio and view node IP information
Test the RX and TX paths and view diagnostic information
Select the waveform for each transceiver
explanation: The Test menu enables testing of the RX and TX paths (including the VA) and viewing versions, network performance and the elapsed time counter; feedback to decision-makers still needs observed delivery. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 58; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 14.

prompt: Which practice does the MANET lesson emphasize when an integrator connects networks?
options: Forward every available report between the networks
Merge the internal designs of both networks
Replace legacy radios before connecting
Limit unnecessary traffic and prevent traffic leakage
explanation: The integrator's best practices are to deny traffic leaking, to apply security and to reduce traffic; the ICD defines the exchange that is actually required. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 70; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: Which element of the Sensor, Decision-Maker, Shooter loop executes the decision?
options: The Sensor
The Decision-Maker
The Shooter
The commander's staff
explanation: Page 7: the Shooter 'acts' by executing the decision. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 7.

prompt: Which sensors belong to the 'Acoustic / RF Detection' group?
options: Thermal Imager and Unmanned Aerial Systems carrying payloads
UAS and SUGV
Thermal Imager and SUGV
Sniper Fire Location Detector and Ground-Based RDF Systems
explanation: Page 15 groups the Sniper Fire Location Detector and Ground-Based Radio Direction Finding Systems under Acoustic / RF Detection. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 15.

prompt: Which of the following is a tactical communication medium?
options: BONTEX, the telephone exchange up to GHQ
PANET, the secured and managed intranet extended to brigades through DBTOCS
HF, VHF and UHF radios, including combat net radio using ROIP
Videoconferencing, cellular and satellite phones
explanation: Page 17 lists HF, VHF and UHF radios and combat net radio as tactical communication; BONTEX and PANET are fixed. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 17.

prompt: Older systems may not be compatible with new sensors. What must be engineered in?
options: Forward encryption of every sensor feed
Backward compatibility
Redundant shielding
Modular licensing
explanation: Page 18 lists legacy integration: older systems may not be compatible with new sensors, so backward compatibility must be engineered in. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: Where is the institutional home for ongoing sensor testing?
options: The Army Signal Regiment's network operations centers
The PA's depot-level and level-4 repair facilities
The Army Intelligence Regiment's ISTAR centers
The using unit's motor pool
explanation: Page 29: the PA's depot-level and level-4 repair facilities assess next-generation technologies and validate technical systems. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: In the sensor, decision-maker and shooter loop, which role does the sensor perform?
options: It detects and collects data from the environment
It analyzes the data, assesses the situation and decides
It executes the decision and creates the desired effect
It directs forces and employs resources for the mission
explanation: The sensor sees by detecting and collecting data; the decision-maker thinks and decides, the shooter acts, and command authority belongs to the organization. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 7; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 7.

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes intelligence from surveillance?
options: Surveillance converts collected information into knowledge; intelligence systematically observes
Surveillance links collection to effects against targets; intelligence systematically observes areas
Intelligence converts collected information into knowledge; surveillance systematically observes
Intelligence and surveillance both mean visual observation by reconnaissance teams
explanation: Intelligence converts collected information into useful knowledge, whereas surveillance is the systematic observation of areas, persons, activities, objects or domains; an RDF bearing is only an observation. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 10; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 8.

prompt: Two networks use different internal technologies. What must be defined at the points where they connect?
options: The entire protocol stack
The internal equipment layout
The users' operating procedures
The password levels of each radio
explanation: At Interoperability Points the whole protocol stack is defined while internal network technologies may differ. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 16.

prompt: Which statement distinguishes quality of service from data overload?
options: QoS concerns competing traffic for limited network resources; data overload concerns more information than operators can process
QoS concerns more information than operators can process; data overload concerns competing traffic for network resources
QoS concerns older systems that are not compatible; data overload concerns different vendor protocols and standards
QoS concerns the cost of the whole network; data overload concerns the training of its operators
explanation: Quality of service is relevant because different traffic competes for limited network resources, while data overload is more information than operators can effectively process. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 9.

prompt: Which measure prevents one equipment failure from compromising the entire system, and which security property does it mainly support?
options: Redundancy, supporting confidentiality
Modular design, supporting confidentiality
Open architecture, supporting integrity
Redundancy, supporting availability
explanation: Redundancy is built in so that the failure of one piece of equipment does not compromise the entire system, which supports availability among confidentiality, integrity and availability. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24.

prompt: Which of the following defines reconnaissance in C4ISTAR?
options: The systematic observation of areas, persons, activities, objects or domains using visual, electronic, photographic, aural or other means
Obtaining information about an adversary's activities and resources or about the characteristics of an area through visual observation or other detection
Detecting, locating and identifying a target with sufficient accuracy and detail to permit effective weapons employment, linking collection to effects
Converting collected information into useful knowledge for commanders, described through the intelligence cycle of planning, collection, processing, analysis and dissemination
explanation: Reconnaissance obtains information about an adversary or an area through visual observation or other detection techniques. The other options define surveillance, target acquisition and intelligence. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 13.

prompt: Which pairing of element and function matches the slide on how the components work as one system?
options: Communications and Computers: transmit, process, integrate and share
Sensors / ISTAR: understand, decide, direct and coordinate for the force
Command and Control: detect, observe, locate and collect in the area
Forces / Shooters: transmit, process, integrate and share with commanders
explanation: Sensors detect, observe, locate and collect; communications and computers transmit, process, integrate and share; command and control understands, decides, directs and coordinates; forces act. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 14.

prompt: Which principle is supported by the statement that standards and profiles reduce integration time and risk?
options: Common standards and interoperability profiles
Standardized Service Interoperability Points (SIOP)
Interface Control Documents (ICD) for each connection
Open architecture of the C4ISTAR framework
explanation: The lesson says standards and profiles reduce integration time and risk while letting existing and future capabilities work together. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18.

prompt: Which of the following describes the D3A process?
options: The process that defines technical standards and profiles for interoperability
An integration process during execution that helps the staff use targeting products
A loop used only for communications planning at the tactical level
The model describing the Army's open architecture and its advantages
explanation: D3A provides a systematic approach to targeting and, during execution, lets the staff use the targeting products to facilitate operations. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 27.

prompt: Which PA-C4ISTAR milestone is described as the operationalization of the PA's first Mobile Command Center?
options: MCC2
MCC3
LRR MCC
MCC1
explanation: MCC1 is the PA's first Mobile Command Center; MCC2 is the second and MCC 3 an additional one. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 30.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT part of the scope of interoperability described in the lesson?
options: People
Processes
Communication information systems
Equipment alone
explanation: Interoperability encompasses people, processes, technology and communication information systems, rather than equipment alone; an ICD defines the technical interfaces. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: Which statement about interoperability and security is correct?
options: Interoperability does not mean unrestricted connectivity; access controls still apply
Once an integrator connects two systems, access controls are no longer needed
Standardized transport removes the need for authentication and authorization
Security is applied only inside each separate network, not between them
explanation: The lesson states that interoperability does not mean unrestricted connectivity, and the integrator connects services without removing the protections that still apply. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 71.

prompt: Before a replacement component is connected, which items does the organization need to understand about the exchange?
options: Who owns the component, when it was bought, what it cost and which unit maintains it afterward
Which waveform it uses, how many nodes join, what key length applies and who holds the passwords
Which unit installs it, which operator uses it, what the training plan is and where it is stored
What information is exchanged, how it is formatted, which interface carries it and how it is interpreted
explanation: The ICD describes the interfaces and information-exchange rules; before connecting a component the organization must know what is exchanged, how it is formatted, what interface carries it and how the receiver interprets it, and modular design keeps compatibility. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 16, 21; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: Which statement correctly relates TCP/IP to voice and data services?
options: TCP/IP integrates voice automatically once data works over the same network
TCP/IP is a standard communication framework, but each service still needs its own verification
TCP/IP replaces the integrator's role in connecting different services
TCP/IP defines the voice and data requirements of each application
explanation: TCP/IP provides a standardized, interoperable framework for communication, while the MANET lesson treats voice and data integration as separate. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 23; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 72, 73.

prompt: Which list contains the four underlying components of the PA C4ISTAR Architectural Framework?
options: Core processes, operational environment, actors and information structure
Core processes, operational environment, actors and communications links
Sensors, decision-makers, shooters and the feedback they provide
Networks, people, processes and command posts of each unit
explanation: The framework represents the relationship of four components: the PA core processes, the operational environment, the actors and the information structure; ASR and AIR are among the actors. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 29; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 27.
